notes: Closest to the reference: Token helpers plus the quoted '{}' fall-through fix, backed by extensive parser, snippet and adapter-level tests; only the site-address suffix check is untouched.
Very close to the reference, including the quoted '{}' guard, with broad tests (some TestParseAll additions only check keys), but it lacks the quoted address-suffix relaxation.

Core fix is correct and includes the suffix tweak, but it adds an unrequested new error for quoted-brace site addresses, misses the '{}' fall-through, and pads the patch with formatter tests for unchanged code.

Fixes the bug with clean Token helpers and skips the address-suffix check for quoted tokens, but it adds an unrequested 'site address cannot be a curly brace' rejection with its own integration test, and it leaves quoted '{}' on a new line glued to the previous segment.
Functionally complete, including the '{}' fall-through, but it repeats inline `Val()==... && !Quoted()` checks everywhere instead of a helper; its parser and dispenser tests are very thorough.
Correct, and it also fixes quoted '{}' on a new line (and tests it), but it repeats inline `&& !Quoted()` checks everywhere instead of a helper, and it misses the quoted address-suffix case.
Correct dispenser and parser fix through Dispenser helpers, but it leaves the quoted '{}' branch skipping the newline-break check; the added formatter tests exercise unchanged code.

Correct core fix via Dispenser helpers with decent dispenser, parse, formatter and integration tests, but it handles neither quoted '{}' segmentation nor the quoted address-suffix check, and it mixes helper and inline styles.

Dispenser-level helpers replace every brace check, including the quoted '{}' fall-through fix the reference makes; the quoted site-address suffix check is left as is; tests cover dispenser, parser and adapt integration well.
Correct fix using Dispenser-level helpers, including the quoted '{}' guard, but it falls back to inline checks in the doImport switch and omits the address-suffix tweak.
Correct, and it includes the site-address suffix fix, but it keeps the quoted '{}' branch short-circuiting; the Token and Dispenser wrapper helpers are slightly redundant.
Correct, and it includes the quoted address-suffix fix, but it adds redundant Dispenser wrappers over the Token methods and does not fix quoted '{}' on a new line.

Clean Token-method helpers that mirror the reference and good parse tests (heredoc, snippet, error case), but it misses the quoted '{}' fall-through and the site-address suffix tweak and adds no adapt test.
Clean, minimal Token-method fix with good parse/dispenser tests including heredoc and an error case, but it handles neither quoted '{}' segmentation nor the address-suffix check.
Clean Token-method approach close to the reference, with a nice integration test covering a matcher plus a real block after a quoted brace; it misses the '{}' and suffix-check refinements.
Clean, focused port of the reference approach using Token methods with solid dispenser, parse and adapt tests, but it does not handle quoted '{}' segmentation or quoted address-suffix checks.
Minimal loop that re-splits the dir per ancestor and always sets Dir; it is correct, if slightly wasteful, and the test covers resources and negative paths.
Works, but it always sets Dir and re-splits and re-joins the path for every slugged ancestor, which is slightly wasteful; the test is strong, with nested slugs, resources and negative assertions.
Works, but writes to segments[count-1] without a bounds check, which is fragile; the test is broad and covers sections, taxonomies, terms and categories.
Functionally correct, but the segment index is written without a bounds check, which is safe only by an implicit invariant; the test is thorough, including terms in a taxonomy without a slug.
Clean recursive slugBase, closest to the reference, with unnormalized handling and a cmp.Or fallback; the test verifies published resources and negative paths.

Mirrors the reference's recursive branch-dir approach with unnormalized handling; its 'only set if different' check is effectively always true for top-level sections, which is harmless, and the test covers resources too.
Recursive slugBaseDir with a found flag, essentially the reference logic layered on the existing Section field; the test also checks term listing permalinks.
Recursive slugBaseDir tracks whether any slug was found and handles path normalization like the reference; the test checks term listings link to the slugged pages.
Simple index-based helper applied to branch and regular pages; the very thorough test covers url overriding slug, nested slugs, and bundle resources; it also updates the docs.
A compact index-based slug substitution feeds an optional Dir override; it is correct, but it also edits docs, and its test barely covers multilingual nesting, though it does check url precedence.
Index-based slug replacement over Ancestors() works but allocates more than needed; also edits the docs, which is reasonable but beyond the reference; the test has good negative assertions.
The Ancestors-based index substitution is correct, but it adds docs edits and its test does not cover nested slugged sections or bundle resources.
Recursive slug-aware section dir builder that mirrors the reference, uses unnormalized paths consistently, handles non-section intermediate dirs, and is tested with nested, plain and term cases.
A recursive slug-dir computation handles disablePathToLower explicitly and only sets Dir when a slug applies, which is close to the reference; the test lacks resource checks.
Replaces segments by index with a bounds check and does a prefix-safe containerDir rewrite in the descriptor; the test covers resources and an intermediate non-section dir.

Replaces segments by index to apply each ancestor section's slug, and uses a boundary-checked prefix swap for leaf container dirs; the test covers nested, non-section intermediate dirs, terms and bundle resources.

Mirrors the reference split (conflict check in getOptions, rewrite after consolidation), deep-copies scenario options, and tests unit, flag-conflict and end-to-end paths including setup/teardown; it lacks lower-layer shortcut dropping and segment conflict checks.

Clean and focused: the conflict check sits in getOptions, applyOnce runs after consolidation and defensively clones maps, and unit plus integration tests are thorough; like the others, it loses a script scenario when env-layer shortcuts override it, which the reference handles.

Well-structured CLI-only Once field with conflicts rejected before the merge, sorted scenario names in the error, and comprehensive consolidation, unit, persistence and integration tests; however, it explicitly codifies env shortcuts wiping script scenarios, which the reference avoids.

Well-structured CLI-only Config field that covers run, archive, cloud and local-execution, with comprehensive consolidation, unit and integration tests; it explicitly accepts that env shortcuts wipe the script scenario rather than dropping them as the reference does.

Works, but it is roundabout: it calls DeriveScenariosFromShortcuts in the no-scenario case, which can error or warn on shortcuts that --once should just discard, and checks the flag via Value.String()=='true'; it also includes unrelated proxy env hacks in test mains.

Works, but detects the flag via Value.String()=="true", needlessly runs DeriveScenariosFromShortcuts for the empty case, checks conflicts only after consolidation, and adds unrelated proxy TestMain hacks.

Clean and focused post-consolidation transform that keeps a default exec unset and clones env and tags, with good unit and integration tests; like most candidates it misses execution-segment conflicts and lower-layer env shortcuts wiping scenarios.

A compact single applyOnceMode called after consolidation, with good table tests and an integration check; conflicts are only detected after consolidation, and lower-layer shortcut overrides are not handled.

Solid design: a CLI-only Config.Once field, conflicts checked before the merge, the raw exec preserved, sorted scenario names in the error, and very thorough tests; scope suffers from a new public GetRawExec on BaseConfig and unrelated proxy-unsetting TestMain hacks in two test packages.

Solid Config-field design that preserves the raw exec and reports conflicts before any merge warnings, with excellent per-command tests, but it adds a public GetRawExec to lib/executor and unrelated proxy-unsetting TestMain hacks in two packages.

Post-consolidation rewrite works for run, archive and cloud, but it adds an exported helper to lib/executor whose error text mentions the CLI-specific '--once', always writes an explicit exec of 'default', and ignores execution-segment conflicts and env shortcuts (e.g. K6_ITERATIONS) that wipe script scenarios.

Functional, but it moves CLI-specific logic, including a "--once" error message, into an exported lib/executor function, its multi-scenario error lacks detail, and it has no cmd-level integration tests.

Functionally correct for the main cases and has good integration tests covering setup/teardown and tags, but it passes two configs awkwardly, sets an explicit 'default' exec, and adds unrelated proxy-unsetting TestMain changes.

Correct transformation with a conflict check on the CLI layer and good integration tests covering setup/teardown and tags, but it always writes an explicit exec and includes unrelated proxy-unsetting TestMain changes.

Context-carried result with proper clearing and an updated fork script is reasonable, but it moves return into the templates namespace, bumps TemplateVersion unnecessarily, silently drops the rest of `return x | f`, and fails namespaced command forms like `return math.ModBool . 2`.

Sound trap mechanism and fork script updated, but it moves return into the templates namespace, bumps TemplateVersion needlessly, wraps the command form only for plain identifiers (not math.Add), and discards nested value returns.

Nice pipeline rewrite (`return a | b` becomes `return (a | b)`) and solid tests. However, try is never taught to re-panic the return sentinel, so `try (return x)` gets swallowed; value returns in defined templates are discarded; and exec.go is edited without a fork-script update.

Nice transform that wraps the whole pipeline as return's argument, but try is not taught to re-panic so try (return x) swallows the return; it also edits exec.go directly and discards value returns across template calls.

The sentinel panic, try passthrough and bare-return output all work, but it hard-codes return-specific AST rewriting into the forked parse.go without updating the fork script (exactly the intrusiveness the issue warns about), and it discards value returns at template boundaries.

Works and has thorough tests, but it patches the upstream parse.go parser to rewrite return pipelines, which is exactly the intrusive fork change the issue warns against; it also edits exec.go without a script change and drops nested value returns.

Passes everything, and its context-based value slot even preserves value returns from defined templates inside partials. However, the slot can leak into nested executions, return values in non-partials and trailing pipeline commands are silently ignored, and errRecover/walkTemplate in exec.go are edited without a fork-script update.

Clean ErrReturn/returnSignal design with the partial value carried in context; it is the only one that keeps a value returned through a template boundary, but it edits errRecover and walkTemplate in exec.go directly and silently drops commands piped after return.

Fork script is updated and namespaced command forms are handled via a special case in evalCall, but it builds a half-initialised CommandNode, silently drops trailing pipeline commands, discards value returns at template boundaries, and includes sizable docs changes.

Follows the reference fork-script approach and handles command-form return in evalCall, but it duplicates the whole walkTemplate body, turns even bare returns into errors that callers must swallow, and discards value returns at template boundaries.

Keeps the HasReturn/io.Discard model, so a partial whose conditional return isn't hit returns nil instead of its output. A bare return inside a defined template ends the whole outer template, and it changes the ExecuteWithContextAndKey signature.

Never traps return at walkTemplate, so a return inside a define or block kills the whole outer template (e.g. baseof); keeping HasReturn with io.Discard makes partials whose conditional return is not hit return nil; it also changes the ExecuteWithContextAndKey signature.

Structurally closest to the reference: fork-script rename, walkTemplate override, and an error for value returns outside partials, plus pipeline reordering. It breaks `return ns.Func args` because only bare identifiers are rewritten, and value returns in defined templates are swallowed.

Closest to the reference semantics (fork-script rename, HasValue, error for value return outside partials), but it copies the walkTemplate body, its moveReturnLast rewrite misses namespaced funcs like math.Add, and it discards value returns from nested templates.

Clean context-based return slot that is cleared for nested executions, with generic arg wrapping. It discards value returns at template boundaries, silently ignores commands after return in a pipeline, patches exec.go walkTemplate without the fork script, and adds doc churn.

Panic-and-trap mechanism with a context-carried result works for the main cases, but walkTemplate drops value returns, anything piped after return is silently ignored, and exec.go is edited directly without updating the fork script.

Fixes same-module blocks and per-instance importConfig and adds good unit and plan tests, but parent blocks still silently override all child blocks for the resource; the transform_config grouping is extra scope.

Fixes the reported same-module case by grouping statements per resource, but still overrides at resource level, so a child module's import of a different instance is silently dropped whenever the parent imports any instance of that resource; the per-instance config tracking and transform grouping are extra scope.

Instance-level static dedupe falls back to resource-level whenever either block is dynamic, so even a for_each import plus a static block in the same module drops the second silently, and module-instance-keyed targets collide.

Static-key dedup compares only the resource key, ignoring module instance keys, and treats any dynamic target as the whole resource, so a static block after a for_each block in the same module, or blocks for different module instances, are silently dropped.

Adds the per-instance first-wins check during expansion like the reference, but its redundant static dedupe compares only the resource key and ignores module instance keys, so blocks for module.child["x"].res and module.child["y"].res are wrongly treated as duplicates and silently dropped.

Has the reference's first-wins check at expansion, but adds a redundant static pre-filter that compares only the resource key, so blocks targeting different module instances (e.g. module.m["x"] and module.m["y"]) are still silently dropped.
Small, clean fix for same-module blocks with a useful slices.Concat aliasing fix, but precedence is still per resource, so child blocks for distinct instances are dropped when a parent block exists.

Same map-of-slices approach as C3 plus a slices.Concat aliasing fix and unit tests, but cross-module override is still per resource rather than per instance, silently dropping a child's distinct-instance imports.

Matches the reference design: all statements are kept, ancestor precedence is resolved per instance, and each instance gets its own import config; it also adds a same-module duplicate error and grouping in transform_config, which are reasonable but extend the scope.

Matches the reference: all statements are kept and resolved per instance at expansion with parent precedence, plus per-instance import config and grouping of unclaimed targets; the new same-module duplicate error is an unrequested behavior change, but tests are thorough.

Keeps every same-module block, which fixes the reported repro, but a parent block still silently drops all child-module blocks for the same resource even when they target different instances, and the added test enshrines that silent drop; the importConfig fix and unclaimed-target grouping go beyond what the task needed.

Fixes the same-module case and tracks per-instance config, but keeps resource-level override and adds a test asserting a child's import of a different instance is ignored (planned as create), which locks in the silent-drop behavior the issue objects to.
Minimal, focused fix with a good table test covering for_each, count, mixed for_each/static and child-module cases, but cross-module precedence still drops child blocks for the whole resource.

Minimal map-of-slices fix with good tests (for_each, count, mixed for_each, child module), but keeps resource-level parent override, so a child's imports of different instances are silently dropped instead of resolved per instance.
Clean slice-based fix that keeps declaration order and all same-module blocks, but it keeps resource-level parent-over-child precedence, so child blocks for distinct instances are silently discarded.

Returns a slice and keeps all same-module blocks, but a separate declaredIn map still drops every child-module block for a resource the parent targets at all, so per-instance semantics are missing; test coverage is thin.

Works and keeps negative-offset validation by also setting OriginalOffset/Range/Step at parse time, but that breaks the literal-vs-expr AST invariant, forcing an addOffsetExpr signature change and a printer reorder; the added reparse round-trip test is strong.

Wraps paren literals with correct paren positions and keeps parse-time Range/Offset values and positive/div/mod validation intact, with a strong reparse round-trip invariant in tests; the extra offset-value plumbing and printer step-order change widen the diff beyond the reference.
Sound wrapping with full paren range (EndPos honored in PositionRange) and positive-duration validation, but misses the Pretty unary-plus fix and div/mod-by-zero look-through.

Solid fix with accurate paren-covering positions and good parse, printer and eval tests; it leaves DurationExpr.Pretty unpatched and div/mod-by-(0) no longer caught at parse time, and the pointer-to-Item parameters are a bit awkward.

Wraps bare literals in a unary-plus Wrapped DurationExpr on both the paren and unary-paren paths, updates Pretty to match String, and keeps parse-time positive and div/mod-by-zero checks by looking through the wrapper; tests are thorough.

Correctly wraps literals in both paren paths and preserves positive/div/mod validation, but the wrapper's StartPos/EndPos point at the literal rather than the parentheses, so error ranges exclude the parens.

Correct wrapping with paren positions and validation look-through including div/mod (via a synthesized negated literal), plus good tests, but does not update DurationExpr.Pretty to drop the unary plus.

Clean fix that wraps literals with paren positions and keeps positive/div/mod validation via an unwrap helper (which returns a synthetic literal on negation); it does not update DurationExpr.Pretty for unary plus.

Cleanly refactors to a single parenthesiseDurationExpr helper (dropping the wrapped flag), updates Pretty and validations, and also moves engine validateOpts after preprocessing so negative-offset checks still fire; that engine reordering is a reasoned but out-of-issue behavior change.

The parser side is a clean unified parenthesiseDurationExpr close to the reference, but it also reorders engine validateOpts/PreprocessExpr in NewInstantQuery and NewRangeQuery, an engine behavior change outside the issue's scope, and its paren positions are literal-based.

Complete fix with prettier and validation updates and very thorough tests (including a direct Prettify test), but PositionRange keys off RHS being a NumberLiteral (fragile for hand-built unary exprs) and Pretty now panics on unexpected ops.

Comprehensive fix and tests (prettier, eval, translate_ast); the PositionRange special case keyed on the RHS being a *NumberLiteral is fragile, the SUB-wrapping code is duplicated, and a panic was added to Pretty.
Minimal, reference-like wrapping on both paths with a positive-duration look-through, but omits the Pretty unary-plus fix and div/mod checks, and the wrapper's range excludes the closing paren.

Focused and correct round-trip fix with a positive-duration check that looks through wrappers; it does not update Pretty or the div/mod checks, and its error ranges like 4:6 for `foo[(0)]` stop before the closing paren.
Fixes String() round-trip, but uses an unconditional $2.(*NumberLiteral) assertion, skips the Pretty unary-plus fix, leaves div/mod-by-zero checks blind to (0), and adds no error-case tests.
Minimal and works, but uses an unchecked `$2.(*NumberLiteral)` assertion in paren_duration_expr, skips Pretty and the div/mod updates, and adds thinner parse-level tests.
